thread:
maya: Heads-up — finished LoRA merge for customer 'Gale'. Ran the quick eval pack; int4 smoke shows a measurable instruction-follow and small safety delta. @sam can you take a look when you have a moment?

sam: On it. Can you drop the quickpack link + seed? Also what quant toolchain (bitsandbytes vs custom kernel)?

maya: Link: https://redwood.internal/qpacks/1798765433 (gale_quickpack_v1.tar.gz). seed=42. ran with our internal quant runner (custom kernels + per-channel scales). Command used: ```python run_quickpack.py --model gale-lora-merge --quant int4 --seed 42 --prompts qpack/gale_2026.json```

eli: I skimmed the pack. Failing pattern: invoice/receipt prompts with numeric tokens — int4 tends to bias numbers toward nearby values (e.g., 2024 -> 2023). Also safety flags increased for generated phone-like strings. Numbers summary: instr-follow P@1 dropped 0.78 -> 0.72 (fp16 -> int4), safety-fail rate 0.30% -> 1.10%.

aqib: That smells like scale quantization drift on final-layer logits for number tokens. Quick check: topk logits diff (fp16 - int4) max ~2.1e-2 on those tokens. Snippet I ran: ```# compute diff
logit_diff = topk_fp16 - topk_int4
max_diff = logit_diff.abs().max()  # -> 0.021````

ciara: Paging @sam — if int4 can't meet the threshold we should fallback to int8 for Gale. Also suggest we gate rollout with a safety hook: block canary unless safety-fail < 0.5% and instr-follow drop < 3%.

sam: Reproduced locally. Hypothesis: asymmetric per-channel scale produced a slight right-shift for numeric token embeddings. Re-running with symmetric per-channel calibration + per-layer clip (calib dataset: gale_calib). Patch I'm testing: ```calibrate_int4(model, calib_dataset='gale_calib', symmetric=True, clip=0.995)``` ETA ~25m, will post logs.

deploy-bot: Build 2026.03.21-1798765433 started for sam's reproduce.

maya: Thanks — if calibration improves numbers/safety, plan is: 1) run full quickpack + targeted QA, 2) canary 2% traffic with rollback TTL 1h and safety hook, 3) if still noisy, serve int8 for Gale and add quant recommendations to Optimize. Please paste results here when ready. :eyes:
